evidence.excerpt: Automated competitive rate monitoring has become a standard component of hotel revenue management, yet the quality of scraped data and the ethical limits of scraping practice receive limited systematic attention in the hospitality literature. This paper conducts a controlled accuracy audit in which rates retrieved by a purpose-built scraping prototype are compared to rates confirmed through direct booking for 48 hotels in Novi Sad, Subotica, and Szeged over a 90-day window totalling 12,960 rate observations. Scraping latency—the delay between a price change and its detection—averages 4.2 hours across the sample, with tails exceeding 18 hours for properties using client-side rendering. Data accuracy is 94.7% at the headline rate level but falls to 81.3% when tax-inclusive rates are required. The paper also reviews applicable terms-of-service restrictions and Serbian and EU legal precedents relevant to automated data collection, providing a compliance checklist for revenue management practitioners.
